t: You're looking at Queen Mary Hall and the YWCA Central Club, together with its railings, in Camden near Bloomsbury. It was designed by Edwin Lutyens. He's the architect best known for imaginatively adapting traditional styles to the needs of his day, and for country houses, war memorials and public buildings. His biographer Christopher Hussey said that in his lifetime he was widely held to be our greatest architect since Wren. The historian Gavin Stamp went further, calling him perhaps the greatest British architect of the twentieth century.
